html:
The 2008 financial crisis was a collapse of banks that began in the US housing market and pushed the world into the deepest downturn since the Great Depression.

In the early 2000s American lenders gave many risky "subprime" mortgages to people who could not afford them. Banks bundled these loans into complex securities and sold them around the world. When house prices began to fall in 2006 and 2007, borrowers defaulted, and nobody knew who held the bad debt.

  • March 2008: the bank Bear Stearns was rescued.
  • 15 September 2008: Lehman Brothers went bankrupt, the largest bankruptcy in US history. Credit froze worldwide.
  • Days later the government saved the insurer AIG, and Congress passed a $700 billion bank rescue.

The Federal Reserve cut interest rates to near zero and printed money to buy bonds. The Great Recession that followed cost millions of jobs and homes. Barack Obama took office in its depths. New bank rules followed in 2010, and the crisis spilled into the European debt crisis. Anger at bank bailouts fed protest movements and populist politics for years.
sum: The 2008 financial crisis was a collapse of banks that began in the US housing market and pushed the world into the deepest downturn since the Great Depression.
